7.Summary description of the proposed organizational change The College of Engineering proposes establishing a standalone Department of Biomedical Engineering Electrical,Computer,and Biomedical Engineering(ECBE).A standalone B ME department will elevate program visibility,strengthen student recruitment and enrollment,support faculty recruitment and retention,and promote stronger research collaborations and industry partnerships.
B.RATIONALE There should be a demonstrable purpose and documented need for the proposed organizational change. 1.
Explain why the organizational change is being proposed.
Biomedical engineering is a rapidly expanding interdisciplinary field bridging engineering, biology, and medicine.URl's B ME program has strong undergraduate enrollment,successful graduates,and faculty conducting nationally funded research in areassuch as wearable bio sensing,brain- machine interfaces,and neural robotics.Despite these successes,the program's administrative integration with EC BE limits its visibility,ability to tailor curricula,and competitiveness in recruiting faculty and students.

Establishing a standalone department will address these limitations, align with industry and workforce needs,and strengthen URl's role in biomedical research and education.
Theneed fora standalone Department of Biomedical Engineering at URl is reinforced by direct feedback from our key stakeholders and comparisons with peer institutions.Our graduates consistently emphasize the value of a clear,independent B ME identity,noting that it would strengthen their professional preparation,enhance visibility for research opportunities,and better position them inthe competitive job market.Similarly,members of research partners have recommended the establishment of an independent department as away to foster stronger industry and academic collaborations, attract high-caliber faculty, and provide a more focused administrative and organizational structure to support growth.

In addition,a review of peer and aspirational institutions shows that independent BME departments are the norm.Remaining administratively within EC BE places URl at a competitive disadvantage in student recruitment,faculty hiring,and research prominence.Creatinga standalone department addresses these gaps, aligning URl with national standards and ensuring the program can continue to thrive as a leader in biomedical engineering education and research.
